published.source: tradeshallglasgow.co.uk/rooms (research/research-room-facts.md, fetched 2026-10-17); the venue's own room plan labels 11.4 m, 7.4 m, 10 m and 5.6 m
published.note: The fields hold the lower section's published figures; the venue also publishes the upper section, 9.7 x 5.6 x 2.18 m, 54.3 m2 (the schema holds one set). Measured: lower section 109.0 m2 of floor, steps 3.1 m2, upper section 52.5 m2, 164.5 m2 in all. The published 11.2 x 7.6 m is the lower section's west wall to the lobby door's casing (11.19 m) by the street wall's face to the shoulders (7.64 m); the room is wider than that south of the lobby door (12.49 m) and deeper in the middle (9.44 m from the street wall's face to the back wall, 9.92 m from the entrance screen). The published 2.8 m is the beams' soffit (2.80-2.83 m); the panels between them are 3.17-3.22 m. Upper section: 5.61 m wide by 9.82 m from the lobby's south wall to the north wall, 2.17 m under its lower ceiling and 2.29 m under the raised field. Drawing and planning use the measured outline; the published capacities are kept (decided 18 October 2026). One room with two floor levels; nothing can be placed on the steps.

transform.note: x = 0.32 - X, y = Z + 3.575, z = Y + 0.04. A proper rotation (det +1), the Grand Hall's quarter turn; the street wall is on -z and +x points 191.1 deg true. The centre is the middle of the outline's bounding box (X -5.938..6.576, Y -11.400..11.327) within 2 mm; it falls on the steps. Floor Z -3.575 is the lower floor's plane at the lower section's centre (-3.5753 by the raster's fit, -3.5751 by plumb lines).

site.note: Derived from the Grand Hall frame constants (tools/grand-hall-survey/README.md, Frame; merchant-city-v2 frame block). This room's quarter turn is the Grand Hall's, so its -z is the Grand Hall's -z, E57 -Y: 101.1 deg true, 102.96 grid, facing Glassford Street. gridOrigin = the Grand Hall's (259332, 665191) + this origin's Grand Hall planner position (x = 8.795 - 0.32 = 8.475, z = -0.04 + 4.963 = 4.923) on +x (-0.22427, -0.97453) and +z (-0.97453, 0.22427). floorODN = 14.19 - 0.045 - 3.575 (the Grand Hall's floor is E57 Z 0.045 at 14.19 m ODN); pavementY = 10.40 - floorODN: the lower floor is 0.17 m above the Glassford Street pavement as the Grand Hall's frame has it (one pavement level for the whole front: its fall along the street is not measured here). The three street openings are one storey below the Grand Hall's windows: their skylines must be recomputed at this height.

ceiling.note: Lower section: a grid of flat-soffited beams (2.799 m under the west one, 2.826 m under the east, 2.81-2.82 m across the middle aisle) with moulded cornices, and eleven flat raised panels between them (3.17-3.22 m). There are no vaults, domes or segmental beams: what read as arches in the panoramas are straight beams in an equirectangular picture. The bays by the street wall (2.795 and 2.808 m), the entrance recess (2.797 m) and the strip by the east wall (2.802 m) are at the beams' level. The height given is the beams' soffit, the venue's published 2.8 m. Upper section: see the upper regions; every height here is above the lower floor.

provenance.method: As the Saloon's and the Reception Room's: plan sections of the reviewed Matterport dollhouse mesh with robust line fits (Tukey IRLS, two passes) per wall face, circles for the curved wall and the columns; vertical sections for the steps; 2 cm depth rasters and photographs re-projected on each opening's plane for the openings; the lowest down-facing surface on a 2.5 cm raster for the ceilings. An independent pass by ray casting (tape lines wall to wall, fans of rays from the 30 stations, plumb lines, level rays at each riser) checked the outline, both floors, the steps and the ceilings. Scripts: tools/surveyed-rooms/measure/robert-adam-room/.
